title: Report variants: save settings and verify reopening
goal: Retain a separate filter variant and distinguish it from an immutable result.

prerequisites.text: 1c-enterprise.a 6; A1–A2: separate infobase, catalogs, references and documents; synthetic data only.

sections.title: From a familiar situation to a checkable question
paragraphs: A saved report variant is not a photograph of a total. It should retain selected settings and read current documents when generated again. Save a separate name for your customer, reopen it in a new session and check an intended one-request change in an experimental copy.

sections.title: Where to act
paragraphs: Work in a new verified copy of your training service. The main Alpha 30/45=75 control and new independent 50/25/15/35/55=180 customer work are different sets. Overall totals include previous work. Nexus saves your note; the standard report and its variants run in external 1C. Do not open unknown EPF/ERF; renaming a variant adds no features.

sections.title: A variant stores settings
paragraphs: A variant retains settings rather than freezing requests. Save a separately named A7 — my customer — minutes for your Alpha. The starter exposes customer/count/minutes; naming a variant cannot add period/status fields. Record the actual code and filter-enabled state.

sections.title: Reason before acting
paragraphs: Follow the scoped native application route; diagrams are not executable browser code.
Identify the infobase, list and particular record separately. A command, visible text and saved state are different things.

sections.title: How to carry out the worked example
paragraphs: Follow the route in your prepared own copy. This is the worked example; the new task below uses different data. Compare each expectation with your actual reread.
Step 1. Select your Alpha by code, enable filtering, generate 2/75 and record parameters. Expected: Settings and 75 identified.
Step 2. Use Save variant/Save variant as with a separate teaching name. Retain the main and other shared variants. Expected: New variant available for selection.

Step 3. Select your variant and check customer code, filter-enabled state and result. If saving is unavailable, record NOT RUN and retain parameters separately. Expected: Settings recovered or limitation explicitly recorded.
Step 4. Change your 30 → 35 in the new copy, regenerate the same variant and verify 80. Preserve source 75. Expected: One changed request explains 80.
Step 5. Record 75/80 with paths / keys / time / settings. Do not promise runtime printing/export restricted by the training edition. Expected: Both states are reproducible.

sections.title: Names should identify the workflow
paragraphs: Do not overwrite the main/shared variant. Use the standard report command to save a new variant, then Выбрать вариант. If this form/edition does not expose personal-variant saving, record that boundary and preserve parameters in your notes; this is not proof of variant persistence.

sections.title: Predict the result
paragraphs: A variant was saved at 180 minutes; one 25-minute request later becomes 30. Must the same variant always display 180?

reveal.title: Check the reasoning
paragraphs: No. With the same reference and membership, a fresh generation gives 185. Keep the earlier 180 result separately with its date and numbers. A variant name alone does not establish a saved filter or immutable documents.

sections.title: Reset and reopen
paragraphs: Close/reopen the report under the same infobase/profile. Compare main and own variants by actual filter, grouping and units rather than title alone. An infobase profile and Nexus account store different state; course self-reports do not replace 1C DCS settings.

sections.title: Context and transitions
paragraphs: Read the path and explain what changes at each step. The diagram does not operate the external application.

sections.title: Check the explanation’s boundary
paragraphs: The result covers the whole set; its title proves nothing.
Retain results/time/keys separately from settings.

sections.title: Archive results separately
paragraphs: In another own copy change one 30-minute request to 35 and rerun the same variant: Alpha becomes 80. That is expected for a saved reference filter. Keep the earlier 75 result separately with date/keys. Do not overwrite accepted work to conceal changed input.

sections.title: A new independent task
paragraphs: Configure the report for your five-request 180 customer and save a new personal variant “A7 — продолжение — минуты”, preserving Default. Close and reopen 1C in the same training infobase and profile; select the variant and check its reference, enabled filter and 180. In your experimental copy change only 25→30, reopen the same variant and generate: expect 185. If your edition’s form offers no saving, record that limit and parameters separately; do not present a note as a saved 1C variant.
Record a prediction first. After your own attempt reveal the reference and compare the selected record as well as its number.

sections.title: Actual training-service window
paragraphs: The author’s separate training copy continues accepted A6: 9/300. Three 30/45/15 requests are added for the main example; the whole copy is 12/390. The main Alpha 75→80 control uses actual DCS. The new independent customer 180→185 is also checked with a saved variant across three 1C processes. OriginalA6 is unchanged; all 12 identities, A4 note, A5 rows and A6 description persist in the copy. Unknown processors were not executed; period/status support is not implemented.

paragraphs: The author’s separate training copy continues accepted A6: 9/300. Three 30/45/15 requests are added for the main example; the whole copy is 12/390. The main Alpha 75→80 control uses actual DCS. The new independent customer 180→185 is also checked with a saved variant across three 1C processes. Technical checks do not assess understanding. Distinguish your observations from unperformed steps. Training names, numbers and comments are fictional; no work data is required.

selfcheck.prompt: A variant was saved at 180 minutes; one 25-minute request later becomes 30. Must the same variant always display 180?
options: No: the same filter should give 185
Yes: a variant stores the old total
Yes: its name prevents data changes
selfcheck.feedback: No. With the same reference and membership, a fresh generation gives 185. Keep the earlier 180 result separately with its date and numbers. A variant name alone does not establish a saved filter or immutable documents.

selfcheck.prompt: After reopening the variant name returns, but another customer is selected. PASS?
options: No: verify the saved reference and enabled filter
selfcheck.feedback: The variant has a separate name and the same customer reference; its filter remains enabled after a new session. Before the data edit five numbers give 180; after changing only 25→30 they give 185. The variant stores a setting rather than the old total. Default is preserved separately; a name or a manually reselected filter alone does not prove persistence. If saving is unavailable, my result is documented parameters and an explicitly unperformed variant check.

selfcheck.prompt: How did you distinguish a setting,saved variant,fresh result and new feature? Give your customer code,numbers,reopened observation and an unperformed step.
selfcheck.feedback: This free response is not graded automatically. Compare it with actual fields in your own infobase.
